dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "31 May 2026 has 17 annual (term_days=365) RENEWALs: DLR-104 (8, $723.42) and DLR-219 (9, $782.87), total $1,506.29."
"Counts/totals equal DF-00020 (8/8 accepted, cash=ledger $723.42, recon=$0) and DF-00040 (9/9, $782.87, recon=$0); effective ranges match."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The spike is posting-date bunching consistent with the month-end annual-file process observed from March onward."
"If the weekly trend pack is built on posted_at, it will look like a close-day jump even though effective dates are spread through May."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The contract-amendment assertion is not independently testable from supplied files."
"Bank/commission cash vs ledger — log cash=ledger is internal. A bank-in mismatch or double commission would change the judgment toward leakage."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not reverse or suppress the 17 postings."
"If none does, add a reversible footnote / dual series to the weekly trend pack: show DLR-104/219 annuals on effective_event_date while retaining posted_at for finance close."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Duplicate revenue — rejected. Global unique source_event_id/recharge_id; the 17 events exist only on 31 May; those subscribers have no other recharge in the extract."
"Decision-changers: a second source_event_id row, non-zero reconciliation, a second 365-day recharge for the same subscriber, or annuals posted on both effective day and 31 May."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No material issue on revenue integrity" is appropriately supported for the tested extract and internal reconciliation, but is broader than the evidence because bank settlement, commissions, entitlement activation, and pre-2026 history were not independently verified.

"Manipulated / opportunistic May close — rejected" is somewhat overstated: the repeated posting pattern and reconciliations weaken that hypothesis, but the submission does not directly test retention-reporting logic or independently verify the dealer process.
"Posted timestamps 21:03–21:46 sit around log posted_at 21:15, consistent with a normal late-evening file drop" is corroborative rather than proof of a normal process.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The strongest alternative was duplicate revenue or a second entitlement/recharge for the same subscriber, including an effective-date posting plus a separate 31 May posting. The analyst explicitly tested unique source_event_id/recharge_id, subscriber repetition, accepted-row counts, and reconciliation totals, while preserving bank, commission, entitlement, and region-mapping uncertainties.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Directly validate the retention-reporting and entitlement pathways: join the 17 events to the dashboard/source metric and CAS activation records, while also confirming DLR-104 and DLR-219 are the only relevant West dealers. This would turn the remaining untested manipulation and customer-impact hypotheses into evidence-based conclusions.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South CareDesk cases fell 187→118 (-36.9%) in the 28-day pre/post windows; comparison regions did not show comparable declines."
"650 South NovaIVR sessions ended at authenticate, including 302 ERROR, 162 ABANDONED and 186 RESOLVED. ivr_interactions.jsonl: filtered region=S, started_at≥2026-05-10, pilot_version=NOVA-S1"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The key measurement problem remains that NovaIVR sessions ending before authentication are excluded from the CareDesk containment denominator."
"NovaIVR caused the decline — not established. The comparison is suggestive, but this is not a randomized test."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Fewer complaints = better CX — rejected. Pre-authentication failures are excluded from the CareDesk denominator."
"Unknowns are what happened after pre-authentication terminations, whether authentication/prompt defects were fixed, whether support demand changed, and whether customers had repeat contacts."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not treat the South case decline as proof that NovaIVR improved customer experience, and do not expand nationally yet."
"Keep NovaIVR limited to South; do not expand nationally yet. Reconcile IVR start → authentication → resolution → transfer → abandonment/error → later contact, including cases absent from CareDesk"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The origin split is important"
"For the 650 South NovaIVR sessions ending at authenticate, what happened to those subscribers afterward?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Pre-authentication failures are excluded from the CareDesk denominator" slightly overstates the cited Farah email, which establishes that pre-authentication sessions are outside the containment denominator but does not necessarily establish that every such failure is excluded from every CareDesk measure.
"South service-event activity did not fall" is supported by continued events and the 17 May signal, but those observations alone do not establish unchanged customer exposure or friction.
The submission reports substantial post-pilot authentication errors and abandonments, but does not demonstrate that these rates increased relative to a pre-pilot baseline.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled simple recorded-channel displacement well, using the origin split to show that the decline was not obviously just IVR cases becoming agent or dealer cases. It only partially handled the strongest benign alternative: lower overall contact demand or other changes in agent/dealer behavior could explain some of the count movement, and IVR abandonment may represent non-complaint behavior rather than hidden dissatisfaction.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quantify the complete pre/post South journey funnel—including authentication errors, abandonments, successful resolutions, transfers, later contacts, and repeat contacts—and compare those rates with a pre-pilot baseline and suitable regions, supplemented by sampled call listening.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites inverter_events.csv fields and states that all four rows were checked.
It explicitly distinguishes the observed absence of another INV-09/TEMP_SENSOR row from the inference that the recovery is unpaired within this small export.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It compares the warning event with the other three events using severity, duration, impact_mw, and cleared fields.
It recognizes that an unpaired recovery may reflect an incomplete extract and proposes checking raw inverter/telemetry history rather than inferring failure from event wording alone.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It assigns Medium confidence because the unpaired status is only an absence within a small extract, while assigning High confidence to directly observed event-field claims.
It limits the conclusion to what the file supports and states a clear stopping point after one cheap check.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to 'verify the raw inverter/telemetry history for INV-09 around 2026-06-04 16:18' is a small, discriminating follow-up.
It appropriately says not to escalate the other rows on this file alone, consistent with zero impact and cleared status.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The scoped conclusion avoids inventing a plant problem from the seven-minute COMM_LINK_WARN event.
It identifies the only reasonable low-cost quality check while preserving the evidence-based conclusion that no material equipment impact is demonstrated.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: 'TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED on INV-09 is the only item worth a cheap check' is a prioritization judgment rather than a directly demonstrated fact, though it is well supported by the reported fields and appropriately limited.

The submission does not independently verify the raw telemetry or establish why the TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED event is unpaired; it correctly presents this as an unresolved possibility rather than a finding of equipment trouble.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The INV-09 recovery may be a normal transient sensor/telemetry condition, or the initiating event may simply fall outside the four-row export. The available zero-impact and cleared fields do not distinguish those possibilities, so the proposed raw-history check is appropriate and no escalation is justified yet.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State explicitly that the raw-history check should look for the initiating temperature-sensor event and any contemporaneous temperature, inverter-state, and power-impact changes; stop if those remain absent or benign.

dimensions.name: A. Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites dispatch_blocks.csv, specific fields, dates, block ranges, and provides the arithmetic for the 31.6% figure: “I summed dsm_penalty_rs across the 96 blocks for each day.”
It identifies schedule_source=pilot_revision for blocks 53–64 and cites the commercial extract for banded absolute-deviation charges.
The claim that no counterfactual is available overlooks the supplied same-day base_schedule_mw and submitted_schedule_mw fields, leaving a central evidentiary path unused.

dimensions.name: B. Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly distinguishes a day-to-day observation from causation: “the claim that the pilot caused a 31.6% reduction is not established.”
It tests weather/operating conditions as an innocent confounder by noting that penalties are concentrated in high-wind periods.
It does not perform the key same-day comparison using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw on 29 May, so its causal diagnosis remains incomplete and it misses the smaller within-day benefit.

dimensions.name: C. Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The claim-specific caveat that 31.6% is not a controlled causal estimate is well calibrated.

However, “the available data does not provide that counterfactual” is overstated: the supplied 29 May base and submitted schedules permit a same-day counterfactual-style estimate, even if it is not a perfect randomized counterfactual.
The submission appropriately identifies uncertainty around weather and operating conditions and avoids treating the observed day-to-day reduction as established savings.

dimensions.name: D. Decision/action quality
citations: “Continue the pilot, but do not expand nationally on the 31.6% claim alone” is a proportionate and operationally safe recommendation.
The proposed matched or alternating high-wind pilot/control blocks, with gusts, schedules, actual output, stow state, and penalties recorded, is a sensible discriminating future test.
The action plan is less effective than it could be because it does not first analyze the existing 29 May same-day base-versus-submitted schedule comparison.

dimensions.name: E. Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly rejects “31.6% proves the pilot caused 31.6% savings” and preserves the valid observation that the selected pilot day had lower total penalty.

It misses a central qualification required by the evidence: the same-day 29 May comparison supports a smaller, nonzero pilot-period benefit rather than leaving the causal question wholly unidentified.
Thus the conclusion is directionally cautious but under-scoped and somewhat overcorrects from the headline claim.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The available data does not provide that counterfactual” is too categorical because base_schedule_mw and submitted_schedule_mw on 29 May can be used to construct a same-day counterfactual-style comparison, subject to residual assumptions.

The statement that the causal effect is entirely unidentified omits the smaller same-day benefit available from comparing conventional/base scheduling with submitted pilot scheduling during the pilot blocks; that estimate still should not be presented as fully randomized causality.

The high-wind concentration claim is labeled medium confidence and is described as “visibly very large” without reporting the actual block-level comparison or quantifying how much of the difference it explains.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% figure is not a causal estimate because it compares different days, but the 29 May block data may still show a smaller positive pilot effect when base_schedule_mw is compared with submitted_schedule_mw for the same pilot-period blocks. The best-supported conclusion is therefore “observed day-level improvement plus a smaller same-day indication of benefit,” not either a proven 31.6% saving or no demonstrated value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Compute and report the 29 May same-day counterfactual-style comparison using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw for blocks 53–64, including the resulting penalty difference and assumptions, before relying on a future matched-control experiment.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The declaration for P1001 uses 90211000 and is for Switzerland, dated 2025-11-04. declaration.pdf, p.1, lines 3–16."

"The Swiss tariff matrix maps P1001 → 90211000, effective 2025-01-01; its owner note says ‘Swiss local nomenclature; confirm Tares/ruling for legal use.’ country_tariff_matrix.xlsx, Swiss Matrix, P1001 row."
"The product master maps P1001 to Helios 90211090, but its Read Me says Helios is the current eight-character value and mappings may be used where a local approved code is not supplied."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"Likely declaration typo/error — rejected for now. The declared 90211000 exactly matches the Swiss Matrix entry for P1001."
"Wrong product/shipment — rejected. P1001 and the product description agree between declaration and invoice, while the AWB links shipment SHP-000522 to declaration CH-2025-000522."
"Helios mismatch proves legal non-compliance — rejected. The Helios value is not sufficient to override the Swiss-specific classification reference."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "Thus the strongest current conclusion is that this is a cross-system code mismatch, not demonstrated declaration error."
"The remaining material gap is the applicable Swiss Tares/ruling entry for P1001 on 2025-11-04."
"both reference workbooks are operational/master-data references, not the final legal ruling source."
"Rejected for now"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "The matrix Read Me says Switzerland uses a local tariff code and that matching strings across jurisdictions is not expected."
"The code-string mismatch therefore appears consistent with different jurisdiction/code systems rather than a proven declaration error."
"The product master maps P1001 to Helios 90211090, but its Read Me says Helios is the current eight-character value and mappings may be used where a local approved code is not supplied."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Run one targeted Swiss Tares/ruling check for P1001 on the declaration date."
"If Tares/ruling = 90211000: close the flag; the declaration code is supported."
"If Tares/ruling = 90211090 or another code: escalate for classification review and possible declaration correction."
"Until that check produces contrary evidence, do not escalate as a likely declaration error."

per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss matrix could be stale, non-authoritative, or not applicable to the product on the declaration date; the declaration could therefore still be incorrect if the authoritative Swiss Tares or ruling entry supports 90211090 or another code. The submission identifies this possibility and makes it the targeted next check.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Provide the actual authoritative Swiss Tares or ruling result, including its effective date and applicability to P1001, rather than relying on the operational matrix pending verification.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "IE-2025-000411 claims Preference = Yes for P1006; declaration date 2025-09-18; declared origin US"
"P1006 invoice is dated 2025-09-18 and states manufacturing country United States"
"Reference search states ‘no current document reference found for SUP-02 / P1006 on 2025-09-18.’"
"Reference file states ‘This does not prove that no document exists outside the register.’"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘US manufacturing proves the preference claim is invalid.’ — Rejected. The invoice establishes manufacturing country, but the applicable preference rule and qualifying origin evidence are still needed."
"‘No current SUP-02/P1006 reference proves no declaration exists.’ — Rejected."
"The SUP-02/P1006 register record ends 2025-07-31, before the shipment, and is marked expired."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The preferential-origin claim is not sufficiently supported for clearance now."
"The reference search also finds no current SUP-02/P1006 document reference, but that result is only a failed lookup, not proof of non-existence."
"a valid document could move the claim from unsupported to potentially supported."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Preference indicator present. Supplier support not linked in ClearView."
"I cross-checked product, date and shipment: the declaration and invoice both identify P1006 / 2025-09-18, and the AWB links SHP-000411 to Ireland."
"ClearView linkage record: a valid linked declaration matching supplier, P1006 and shipment date would close the current evidence gap."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Safe now: hold preferential treatment pending supplier-document and rule verification."
"Clear only if those records establish valid preferential origin for P1006 on 2025-09-18; otherwise correct/escalate the preference treatment."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission does not cite the governing preference agreement or rule establishing the exact documentary requirements for clearance; its conclusion is therefore appropriately limited to insufficient current support rather than a legal finding that the claim is invalid.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Preferential origin may still be valid despite the invoice stating United States manufacturing, if a separate supplier declaration or qualifying production/origin rule supports the claim. The expired SUP-02 register entry and failed ClearView lookup do not exclude that possibility; they establish an evidence and linkage gap, not fraud or definitive invalidity.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Cite and apply the governing preference rule to the product and obtain the shipment-dated supplier declaration or equivalent origin evidence, explicitly reconciling it with the expired SUP-02 record and any alternative supplier record.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "batch_release.csv: disposition, receipt_ts, qcore_release_ts; calculated on RELEASED rows."
"source_freshness.csv: source, snapshot_ts, typical_refresh, notes."
"qc_release_sop.md: Standard flow and Service target."

"No negative receipt→release interval or lab-complete-after-release ordering error was found." — Key claims are tied to relevant files and fields, though the submission does not provide row-level examples or the hourly timestamp profile and gives limited counterevidence.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The SOP does not define the 24h target from receipt, and upstream snapshots have different freshness."
"Therefore some status fields may be stale relative to QCore and contaminate interpretation of an apparent cycle time."

"The timestamp arithmetic is broken — rejected. The extract contains no negative receipt-to-release intervals and no lab-complete-after-release ordering failure." — It identifies important definitional and snapshot confounding, but treats ordering checks as insufficiently strong evidence against timestamp/interface-semantic problems and does not test the 02:10 release-time concentration.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Therefore some status fields may be stale relative to QCore and contaminate interpretation of an apparent cycle time. ... Medium"
"Do not use the apparent ‘1.5 day’ receipt-to-release time as a performance KPI yet."

"If a material share of routine batches is >24h, treat the delay as a genuine performance issue" — Confidence is generally claim-specific and appropriately recognizes source freshness, although it does not bound the impact of the timestamp/interface artifact or the non-synchronous join.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not use the apparent ‘1.5 day’ receipt-to-release time as a performance KPI yet."
"Ask for the SOP-defined required-evidence-available timestamp for the released batches. Then calculate qcore_release_ts − evidence_available_ts."

"If that interval is generally ≤24h, reframe the dashboard around the SOP-defined cycle." — This is a useful, reversible reframing with a decision threshold, but it should also protect against interpreting a new join as valid without aligned snapshots or a true decision event timestamp.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The timestamp arithmetic is broken — rejected."
"Missing QCore timestamps make the released population incomplete — rejected."

"The 39–45h receipt-to-release result proves poor QC performance — rejected." — Multiple alternatives are considered, but the strongest competing explanation—interface commits or scheduled batch releases rather than decision times—is not tested, and the rejection of timestamp problems relies mainly on ordering checks.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "The decisive next check is therefore to obtain the SOP-defined required-evidence-available timestamp and compare it with qcore_release_ts."

"Ask for the SOP-defined required-evidence-available timestamp for the released batches." — This requests a small, high-value discriminator, but omits the event/decision timestamp definition or event log and does not request a source-aligned snapshot.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The timestamp arithmetic is broken — rejected" is overstated: absence of negative intervals or obvious ordering errors does not establish that qcore_release_ts represents the operational decision time.

"Therefore some status fields may be stale relative to QCore" is a plausible inference from freshness metadata, but the submission does not demonstrate the magnitude or direction of the resulting bias.
The proposed qcore_release_ts − evidence_available_ts calculation implicitly assumes those fields can be joined across extracts despite the stated non-synchronous snapshots.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent 39–45 hour cycle may primarily reflect QCore interface or scheduled release commits, especially if qcore_release_ts is heavily concentrated at 02:10, rather than elapsed time from the QC decision. Non-synchronous QCore, LabTrack, and CertVault extracts could further distort an evidence-available join.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Profile qcore_release_ts by hour and obtain an event-level, source-aligned record defining both required-evidence availability and the actual disposition decision (or interface commit). Use that evidence to distinguish workflow delay from timestamp/interface timing before calculating or operationalizing the KPI.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "24 requests total $152,558.03" tied to part_requests.csv, PR-260700–PR-260723, and external_quote_usd.
"Actionable bucket = $17,315.58" tied to specific request IDs and matching manufacturer_part_no, revision, uom, availability, and restriction rows.
"The freshness calculation uses the latest QCore snapshot of 2026-07-31 02:10" with source-specific ages reported.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Continue the semantic-search pilot, but use it for candidate discovery only."
"MPN/revision/UOM, quantity, reservation and receiving-site qualification remain the transfer gates."
The submission tests separate failure modes using the exact-match-but-critical-reserved example and the insufficient-quantity examples.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Global availability is only a screening signal" and "final transfer approval should use current local confirmation."
The submission quantifies the three buckets and reports MaintStar-global as approximately 35 days old.
The labels "High" for actionable totals somewhat overstate certainty because the underlying global availability snapshot is stale and local confirmation has not yet occurred.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: The recommendation reframes semantic search as candidate discovery rather than automatic transfer approval.
"For the $105,532.53 engineering bucket, obtain missing MPN/configuration evidence" and for the non-transferable bucket obtain "fresh local reservation/availability confirmation."
The proposed gates are operationally protective, although explicit pilot success criteria and a time-boxed validation design are not stated.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Semantic similarity means safe transfer. Rejected" using PR-260712, which exactly matches MTR-4401/A but is reserved for a critical asset.
"Global available quantity means free stock. Rejected" because restrictions separately record critical-asset reservations.
The submission states what evidence could move engineering and non-transferable items into the actionable bucket.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: It requests missing MPN/configuration evidence for the engineering bucket and fresh local reservation/availability confirmation for the non-transferable bucket.
It specifies the decision impact: confirmed MPN/revision/UOM plus qualification and free-stock confirmation can move an item to actionable.
The requests are relevant and prioritized by bucket, though the submission does not identify the single highest-value item or owner/query for obtaining the evidence.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The "Actionable now" classification and its High confidence are stronger than the evidence supports while global availability is based partly on a roughly 35-day-old MaintStar-global snapshot and local confirmation is still pending.

The engineering bucket is labeled High confidence even though it explicitly depends on missing MPN/configuration evidence; the bucket assignment may be reliable, but transferability is not yet established.

The statement that confirmed free and sufficient stock can move an item to actionable should also retain revision, UOM, qualification, and any other restriction checks rather than treating local availability alone as sufficient.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic-search results may identify genuine operational equivalents, but the apparent $17,315.58 actionable value could be materially lower—or temporarily unavailable—because the joined inventory and restriction data are not a coherent current-time snapshot. The more defensible present conclusion is candidate value, with actionable value pending local confirmation and engineering validation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Re-run the eight purported actionable matches against a single current local CMMS/reservation extract, retaining MPN, revision, UOM, quantity, qualification, and reservation fields; report the conversion rate from candidate to approved transfer and use that result to recalibrate the $17,315.58 actionable estimate.
